newsitem.title: USA: Clinton warns against balanced budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton warns against balanced budget amendment.

text.p: President Clinton warned Congress on Tuesday against amending the Constitution to require a balanced budget, saying that this could "cripple our country in time of crisis."
"Balancing the budget requires only your vote and my signature. It does not require us to rewrite our Constitution," Clinton said in the prepared text of his State of the Union speech.

Republican congressional leaders, who fell just one vote short of passing a balanced budget amendment last year, have vowed to make it the first order of legislative business in the new Congress. The Senate is expected to begin debate on the amendment on Wednesday.

"It is unnecessary and unwise to adopt a balanced budget amendment that could cripple our country in time of crisis later on, and force unwanted results such as judges halting Social Security checks or increasing taxes," Clinton said in his speech to Congress and a national television audience.
"We don't need a Constitutional amendment -- we need action," he said, adding, "We must move quickly ... to balance our budget."
The president said he will propose a detailed plan on Thursday to balance the budget by the year 2002.
The plan will protect the Medicare and Medicaid health care programs, education and the environment. It will also provide middle class tax relief, he said.

"Whatever our differeneces, we should balance the budget now, and then, for the long-term health of our society, we must agree to a bipartisan process to preserve Social Security and reform Medicare," Clinton
